title: The School Run
strapline: Buggy, car seat, scooter or walk — the everyday journey every child already knows by heart.
intent: Children replay a journey that is deeply familiar, making sense of their own daily routine through play.
Children sequence the morning — coats, bags, buckle up, wave goodbye, arrive — and hold the order confidently.
Children use the language of their own transport — buggy, car seat, bus pass, scooter, zebra crossing.
Children act out care and belonging: strapping in the babies, finding the book bag, saying goodbye and hello.
Children talk about how they get to nursery and notice that friends come different ways.
implementation: Provide dolls, buggies, car seats and bags so children can pack up and set off exactly as they do at home.
Take part as the person being dropped off or collected, following the child's version of the routine.
Narrate the sequence: 'Coats on, bags packed, into the car seat, click — off we go!'
Add a zebra crossing and a lollipop person and rehearse stop, look, listen, cross.
Provide book bags, water bottles and a peg with each child's name to find and hang.
Talk warmly about goodbyes and hellos — the wobble at drop-off, the joy at pick-up.
Chart how children travel to nursery — walk, bus, car, scooter — and count each way.
key_questions: How do you get to nursery in the morning?
What do we need to pack before we leave the house?
What comes first — coats or shoes? And then what?
How do we cross the road safely at the zebra crossing?
Who buckles the baby in, and how do we know she's safe?

impact.text: Children replay the drop-off journey in role, strapping in babies and packing bags with care.
Children recount and sequence their own morning routine, keeping the order.
Children use the words of their own transport and journey — buggy, car seat, crossing, bus.
Children rehearse crossing safely — stop, look, listen — with the lollipop person.
Children act out goodbyes and hellos and talk about the feelings that come with them.
Children notice that friends travel to nursery different ways and count each way.

enhancements: Dolls, buggies, slings and car seats to strap and unstrap.
Book bags, water bottles and a name-peg for each child to find.
A taped zebra crossing and a lollipop-person sign.
A row of chairs as the car or bus, with click-in seatbelts (scarves).
A drop-off door with a wave-goodbye window.
Photos of how each child travels in — walk, bus, car, scooter.
A morning-routine picture sequence to put in order.

playing_exploring: Children play out what they know best — their own morning — and make sense of it.
They bring real feelings about drop-off and pick-up into the game.
active_learning: Children see the whole journey through, from packing to arrival.
They practise the fiddly bits — buckles, bags, pegs — until they master them.
creating_thinking: Children sequence and re-sequence the routine and notice when a step is missing.
They solve the everyday problems — the lost shoe, the forgotten bag — in play.
